test_title: SSC CGL (2022) Tier-II Official Paper (Held On : 3 March 2023)
subject: general
question:
Three Statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some poems are horses.

All horses are toys.

All toys are ships.

**Conclusions:**

I. All toys being poems is a possibility.

II. Some horses are ships.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Either conclusion I or II follows.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5ebc895cac8edb31d148d0ec9c354cd0b3080eb7dfd496ede1a493d5e970f898.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All toys being poems is a possibility → follow (The given conclusion is not definite but there is possibility applied in it. So, false conclusion with possibility will be considered as true conclusion, Hence, it is true.)

II. Some horses are ships → follow (As all horses are toys and all toys are ships. So, all horses comes in toys which whole comes in ships therefore it is definitely true)

∴ Here, Both conclusions I and II follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is **"Both conclusions I and II follow**"
